title: Struktly Record bundle
description: One sealed Struktly Record, exported so that somebody who does not run Struktly can check it. The manifest describes the sealed bytes; `sealed` carries those bytes verbatim. This document is the compatibility contract between whatever produced the bundle and whatever verifies it: a producer must emit exactly this shape, and a verifier may rely on it.

sealed.description: The sealed payload exactly as it was sealed, carried raw. A verifier hashes these bytes and compares the result with manifest.payload_sha256, so re-encoding this value — reordering keys, changing whitespace — breaks verification even though the meaning is unchanged.

exported_at.description: When the bundle was made. Deliberately outside the hashed payload: exporting a Record must not change it, so two bundles of one Record differ here and verify identically.

manifest.description: What a verifier checks the payload against.

revision.description: Which sealed revision this is. Revisions start at 1; a superseded revision remains exportable and verifiable after a later one exists.

disposition.description: What the Record says became of the work.

payload_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the sealed bytes, lowercase hexadecimal. This is the whole of what a verifier can check by arithmetic.

evidence_sha256.description: Digest of the evidence snapshot taken at seal time, where one exists. Optional, and the absence is meaningful rather than an omission: an execution with no evidence document, or one whose evidence could not be read when the Record was captured, seals without this field and records the reason as a capture limitation inside the payload. A verifier must therefore treat a missing key as 'no evidence snapshot was hashed', never as an invalid bundle.

evidence_embedded.description: Whether the evidence snapshot's contents travel in this bundle. Always present, because a bundle that carries only a hash must say so — an omission a reader has to interpret is the thing this field exists to prevent.

judgements.description: Conclusions carried inside the sealed bytes. The property is optional only for v1 Records sealed before judgement snapshots existed. When this object is present, empty arrays mean the producer evaluated that category and found none; they are not unknown.

compliance.description: The recorded compliance verdict, or null when no compliance verdict was recorded.
